title: Critical time step computation
objective: Compute the critical time step for the central-difference integrator via the Courant condition: dt_crit = L_min / c_d where L_min is the minimum element characteristic length and c_d is the dilatational wave speed.
scope: Add `mechdsl.solver.critical_timestep(coords, conn, lam, mu, rho, safety=0.9)` returning the Courant-limited stable time step.
Characteristic length = element volume^(1/3) for Hex8; element-shortest-edge for tets.
Dilatational wave speed: c_d = sqrt((lam + 2 mu) / rho).
Per-element dt is min over all quadrature points; global dt is min over all elements; apply safety factor.
Expose in the generated explicit driver: `dt_crit = critical_timestep(...)` as a helper function.
implementation_steps: Inline the helper in the emitted explicit driver.
Unit-test on a regular unit-cube Hex8 mesh with known wave speed.
acceptance_criteria: Regular unit-cube mesh: computed dt matches L/c_d within 1e-8.
Irregular mesh: dt is below the min-element limit (safety check).

cases: Irregular mesh dt below per-element min

risks: Nonlinear wave speed (strain-stiffening materials) makes dt state-dependent. Mitigation: recompute dt periodically in the explicit driver (e.g. every 100 steps) rather than once.
completion_notes: Char length convention: Hex8 = V^(1/3) via 2x2x2 Gauss (reuses lumped_mass.py Jacobian machinery); Tet4/Tet10 = shortest corner edge
